title: Model-aware cache sculpting and batching strategies for long-context LLaMA/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Customer workloads are increasingly sending long-context requests (16K–64K tokens). Existing generic memory profiles lead to high GPU fragmentation and conservative allocation for LLaMA/Mistral/Qwen variants. This ticket scopes a model-aware approach to reduce peak GPU footprint while preserving latency SLOs by combining: (1) cache sculpting (fine-grained per-layer KV residency policies), (2) KV condensation (lightweight compression for older KV entries), and (3) sequence-aware batching/packing that respects per-variant memory shapes. Objectives: 1) Reduce 32K/64K peak memory per-request by at least ~18% compared to current default memory profile for target variants. 2) Maintain p95 generation latency within 5% of baseline on 4K workloads. 3) Integrate with continuous batching to avoid throughput regressions. Scope: - Target variants: LLaMA-2-70B (instruct), Mistral-8x (long), Qwen-14B-instruct (long-ctx tuned). - Focus on server-side runtime components (allocator, KV manager, batcher) and offline profile generation pipeline. Not in scope: tokenizer or model architecture changes. Approach: - Collect representative long-seq traces (customer anonymized + synthetic). - Run a param sweep simulator (existing mem-sim harness) to generate candidate per-variant memory knobs: per-layer residency thresholds, condensation windows, slice sizes for shard-aware packing. - Implement a runtime plugin that applies model-aware knobs at request time: a) temporal priority eviction (recent tokens pinned, older cross-layer entries eligible for condensation/eviction), b) on-the-fly light compression for cold KV slices (FP16 delta + run-length style packing), c) batch coalescing policy that prefers packing requests with similar seq-length distributions to reduce wasted KV allocations. - Safety: conservative fallback to current profile on any anomaly; metrics and canary gating before rollout.
acceptance_criteria: 32k/64k peak memory reduction >= 18% for each target variant in lab traces
p95 latency on standard 4k workload increases <= 5% compared to baseline runtime-1.21
No correctness regressions for chat-stateful scenarios (regression suite pass)
Automated canary rollout configuration in console with telemetry and automatic rollback

notes: Trade-offs: aggressive KV compression reduces memory but increases CPU and potential latency; per-layer policies add complexity to rollout/observability. Decision: start conservative, expose knobs per-customer tier, and gate model-specific aggressive profiles behind dedicated capacity where CPU budget is known. Follow-up: if prototype stabilizes, extend to automated profile generation for new variants via continuous trace ingestion.
